text: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) is a database of traditional knowledge from Indian medical systems - Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Yoga. It contains over 3.5 lakh (350,000) formulations from 150+ classical texts. TKDL converts traditional knowledge from Sanskrit, Hindi, Arabic, Persian and Urdu into patent-compatible format in five international languages (English, German, French, Spanish, Japanese). It was created to prevent biopiracy and misappropriation of Indian traditional knowledge through patents.

TKDL serves as prior art for patent examination. Patent offices in the US, EU, UK, Japan, Australia and others have access agreements with TKDL. When a patent application claims an invention based on traditional Indian knowledge, examiners search TKDL to check if the claimed invention is already documented. If found in TKDL, the patent can be rejected for lack of novelty or obviousness. As of 2023, TKDL evidence has been cited in over 250 patent cases, preventing grant of patents on traditional knowledge.

Before filing a patent application on any AYUSH-related invention, you should: (1) Search TKDL database to check if your formulation or concept is already documented; (2) If your invention is based on a traditional formulation, clearly identify what is novel - the modification, new use, or improvement; (3) Document how your invention differs from traditional knowledge with scientific evidence; (4) Be prepared to explain why your invention involves inventive step over known traditional formulations.

TKDL is not publicly accessible. It is available only to patent examiners at international patent offices under access agreements to prevent misuse. Applicants cannot directly search TKDL. However, you can: (1) Search classical Ayurvedic texts directly (many are available in digital format); (2) Consult Ayurvedic experts to verify if your formulation is traditional; (3) Search the Ayush Research Portal and published Ayurvedic pharmacopoeia; (4) During patent examination, examiner may cite TKDL references which you can then review.

Major classical texts included in TKDL for Ayurveda: Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, Ashtanga Sangraha, Bhavaprakasha, Sharangadhara Samhita, Chakradatta, Yogaratnakara, Rasatarangini, and Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India. Any formulation described in these texts is prior art and not patentable as such. However, modifications showing enhanced efficacy with clinical evidence may be patentable.

TKDL has prevented biopiracy attempts including: (1) Turmeric patent (US5401504) for wound healing - revoked 1997; (2) Neem patent (EP0436257) for fungicidal use - revoked 2005; (3) Basmati patent (US5663484) - partially revoked; (4) Over 200 other patents challenged or withdrawn. For AYUSH entrepreneurs, this means: document your innovation clearly to distinguish from traditional knowledge, and ensure your patent claims focus on genuinely novel aspects.
